title: New Residential Construction — Building Permits, Housing Starts and Housing Completions (August 2026 data), 8:30 a.m. ET — the nowcast ladder's middle rung, and the corridor's loudest starts vintage of 2026:Q3
source: CENSUS: four independent census.gov primaries, all fetched direct 2026-09-06. (1) economic-indicators/calendar-listview.html (HTTP 200, 91,396 bytes, 179 table rows parsed), row "New Residential Construction (Building Permits, Housing Starts, and Housing Completions) | September 17, 2026 | 8:30 AM | August 2026", release code A202609170830, reference A202608; the page's only four Suspended rows are Preliminary Steel Imports x2 and the Advance Economic Indicators Report x2, none this series. (2) construction/soc/schedule.html (HTTP 200, 59,625 bytes), the Survey of Construction's own program calendar, row "August 2026 | September 17, 2026 | September 24, 2026" under the column heads "(12th Workday) New Residential Construction - 8:30 a.m." and "(17th Workday) Revised Building Permits - 8:00 a.m. / New Residential Sales - 10:00 a.m." (3) construction/xls/historic_release_dates.xls (HTTP 200, 55,808 bytes; 514 reference months 1984-01 -> 2026-11), reference 2026-08 -> NRC 2026-09-17, NRS 2026-09-24. (4) The STANDING release itself — construction/nrc/pdf/newresconst.pdf (HTTP 200, 322,067 bytes), CB26-127, July 2026 data, whose own front page reads "Next Release: September 17, 2026". Promoted this session from the EST: proposal on the two-primary precedent this calendar carries for durable-goods-2026-11-25, m3-full-report-2026-12-03 and housing-starts-2026-10-20; four primaries is one more than any of them. Corroborated by a non-Census source: the Atlanta Fed's GDPNowcastDataReleaseDates.xlsx PostedUpdates sheet (HTTP 200, 16,944 bytes, 82 dated rows 2025-12-23 -> 2026-12-23), whose 2026-09-17 08:30 row reads "Housing starts" and nothing else. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: The nearest edition of a series the 12-17 lane DECLINED as "not distinguishable" and the 10-20 lane called "dirty". Initial research 2026-09-06 at D-11 found it distinguishable in both places, and in the opposite direction from 10-20 on the nowcast. THE LADDER (Leg 2): the 10-20 lane split GDPNow's ContribArchives (10,875,424 bytes; 1,871 vintages 2014-05-01 -> 2026-07-28 = 1,822 same-quarter deltas) into in-quarter 0.0869pp (n=95) vs post-quarter 0.0250pp (n=48), a 3.48x step, and offered but explicitly did not test a mechanism — "the third month lands in an already-observed quarter". That mechanism predicts a monotone gradient, not a step, and the gradient is here: starts vintages land at exactly THREE positions per nowcast quarter, and the median |delta residential| falls monotonically across them — R1 (dq -45..-19, release months 02/05/08/11) n=48 at 0.1020pp, R2 (dq -15..-5, months 03/06/09/12) n=47 at 0.0726pp, R3 (dq +9..+57, months 01/04/07/10) n=48 at 0.0250pp; p(R1 vs R2)=0.038 and p(R2 vs R3)<0.0001 on 20,000-iteration permutations. Both natural controls show a HUMP rather than a decline — pooled non-starts 0.0056/0.0105/0.0049 (p(R1vR2)=0.011) and construction spending on its own three positions 0.0369/0.0776/0.0632 (p(C1vC2)=0.013, p(C2vC3)=0.247) — so the monotone decline is this release's own signature. 2026-09-17 08:30 is an R2 vintage (dq -13, SOLO on PostedUpdates), the LAST in-quarter starts vintage of 2026:Q3, so the number to carry is 0.0726pp pooled or 0.0650pp on the tightest matching cut (R2+solo, n=35) — both ABOVE the corridor's unconditional 0.0609pp, the opposite direction from the 10-20 finding. It is also the FIRST out-of-sample instance of the whole gradient, scoring 33 days before the 10-20 lane's own test. Attribution is high but not perfect: R2-solo puts residential largest 33/35 = 94.3% against a 20.7% base rate, versus R3-solo's 35/35. THE TAPE (Leg 3): the release-day study was re-run independently from Census's 514 dates on Yahoo bars and reproduces the siblings exactly (ITB 0.575% vs 0.447%, n=239, p=0.0015; 2021-26 null 0.543/0.486, p=0.45). The "dirty" label was then measured against 167 scheduled FOMC decision days reconstructed from federalreserve.gov's own historical calendars, and its stated reason is wrong: on the 10 release days in 20 years that fell the session after an FOMC decision ITB's gap is 0.539% vs 0.576% (p=0.875), opex eve is null (0.565% vs 0.575%, n=42, p=0.936), and September release days are QUIETER (0.346% vs 0.576%, p=0.205). What survives is a calibration problem, not a widening: the exact 2026 configuration (after-FOMC AND opex-eve) has occurred 7 times, clearing the corridor's 1.579% threshold 2 of 7, and the after-FOMC release set clears it 3 of 10 against the 10% a p90 implies (binomial p~0.07) — with only n=3 in the 2021-26 era that set the threshold. So this date's ITB gap is uninformative in BOTH directions and must not be scored as a kill-switch observation; 10-20 remains the clean instance. THE CONTENT (Leg 4), the first leg in this corridor about what the print will SAY: July 2026 starts printed 1,239,000, -12.4% (+/-9.5%), and after a m/m drop of 10% or more the next month is positive 15 of 17 post-2010 (median +8.35%, implying ~1,342K) and 56 of 73 full-history, against a 52.8% unconditional rate — but the symmetric control kills the economic reading, since after a +10% rise the next month is negative 26 of 30 (median -8.56%) and the lag-1 autocorrelation of m/m is -0.406. It is mechanical mean reversion in a survey whose own 90% interval is +/-9.5%, reliable and meaningless. impact low and symbols [] are re-derived here, not inherited: no macro- or housing-keyed house playbook exists (housing re-grepped 2026-09-06 across trade-playbooks.md and multi-symbol-sweep.md, 0 hits) and no instrument attaches. Cliff exposure is nil — all 9 of 514 out-of-month slips since 1984 are funding-lapse slips, the 09-30 deadline is AVERTED (PL 119-103 funds through 2026-12-11), and D-11 puts this print 85 days ahead of the successor cliff. Date confirmed on four Census primaries; that licenses nothing and the call is stand aside on every horizon. Discovered in the construction-spending-2026-10-01 adjacency sweep 2026-09-06; canonical file written by this event's own initial research the same day, which shadows that proposal.
